title: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | US Stock Market Today | Live: S&P 500, Nasdaq futures rise as tech stocks provide a boost - The Economic Times
text:
Dow Jones Today | US Stock Market Live: Concerns over the ⁠payoff from AI ‌investments have battered chip stocks recently, but robust quarterly results and forecasts signaling resilient demand have brought ​the tech-heavy Nasdaq closer ​to record highs.

Markets will closely watch Nvidia’s results next week for signs that the technology-led rally can continue. Shares rose 0.6% after a report said the chipmaker had scaled back plans to support a proposed OpenAI data centre project in Ohio, easing concerns about circular financing in the AI sector.

Middle East tensions remained elevated after Iran urged the US to accept defeat and President Donald Trump warned Americans to prepare for persistently high fuel prices. Investors will also turn to earnings from Walmart and Home Depot later this week.

A string of mild inflation reports and an unexpected decline in retail sales reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September, helping the S&P 500 reach a record high last week. Traders now see a 31% chance of a 25-basis-point increase, down from roughly even odds a week earlier, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Technology stocks rose in premarket trading after Reuters reported that IPO-bound Anthropic expects revenue to reach roughly $190 billion to $200 billion in 2028. Amazon gained 1.2%, Alphabet added 0.6%, Micron Technology climbed 3% and Broadcom rose 1.1%.

S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures advanced on Monday after AI company Anthropic issued a strong revenue forecast, boosting technology stocks. Investors also weighed expectations of fewer Federal Reserve rate hikes against continuing Middle East tensions.

At 7:32 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis fell 90 points, or 0.17%, while S&P 500 E-minis rose 10.5 points, or 0.13%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis gained 156.75 points, or 0.52%.
